reasoning: The PR makes NULL cells render as a muted 'N/A' and stops rendering empty strings as 'N/A'. Rendered on both branches with the same story data (four extra rows covering a NULL value, an empty string, a missing column key, and a NULL numeric), the only differences are the intended ones. NULL cells: base paints 'N/A' at full body-text strength (rgba(0,0,0,0.88) light, rgba(255,255,255,0.85) dark); the PR paints it at colorTextTertiary (rgba(0,0,0,0.45) -> composited #8c8c8c light, rgba(255,255,255,0.45) -> #737373 dark) and adds the dt-is-null class only to those cells. That is exactly the classic table plugin's treatment (plugin-chart-table/src/Styles.tsx: '.dt-is-null { color: theme.colorTextTertiary }'), which is the stated alignment target, and the colour comes from a theme token in both themes. Empty-string cells: base showed a misleading 'N/A'; the PR renders them blank, so an empty string is now visually distinct from a NULL. Every non-NULL cell is byte-identical in text, computed colour and background across the two branches in both themes, and no other part of the chart (header, search box, cell bars, zebra striping, row heights) changed. Contrast of the muted placeholder measures 3.36:1 in light and 4.43:1 in dark against the row background. Light is below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 body-text threshold, but this is a deliberate de-emphasis of a placeholder rather than data, it is the exact value the classic table has always used, and it stays above the 3:1 non-text/large-text floor; the muted text is clearly legible in the screenshots. On that basis the rendered result is not worse than the base branch.

Contrast ratios are WCAG relative-luminance ratios of the alpha-composited text colour against the row background (white in light, black in dark).
